Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

frequent adjective

also repeated, constant (frequent), regular (often there), a frequent visitor

classical

Caes. BG 5.45: tantō crēbriōrēs litterae nūntiīque (Lewis & Short)
Cato Agr. 48.2: crēbrō runcātō

crēber, crēbra, crēbrum

adjective; comparative crēbrior; adverb crēbrō, often

frequent, repeated; close-set

Of things that come one after another: letters, blows, rumours, visits. Of things in space it means thick, close together (crēbrae arborēs), the opposite of rārus.

Other words

  • frequēns, frequentis — frequent; often present; crowded

    adjective, third declension, one ending; adverb frequenter · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 16: erat ille Rōmae frequēns (Lewis & Short); Cic. Or. 4.45: frequēns … Platōnis audītor (Lewis & Short)

    Of a person who is often in a place or often does a thing, a regular (frequēns audītor, a regular listener). Its other common sense is crowded, full (frequēns senātus, a full senate; Liv. 1.9.9, a city frequentem tēctīs).

Examples

  • signumque aput tāleam adpōnitō crēbrōque sarītō, sī volēs citō sēmina crēscant

    put a marker by the cutting and hoe often, if you want the seedlings to grow fastCato Agr. 46

  • tū tamen quam frequentissimē scrībe

    do write as often as you canPlin. Ep. 6.7.3

  • cum situm moeniaque et frequentem tēctīs urbem vīdissent

    when they had seen the site, the walls and the city full of housesLiv. 1.9.9

See also often, every so often, whenever.
